english: Whatever content once filled this chamber has been pushed up against the cracked walls.
The dwarven masonry is damaged in various locations and everything, every single thing in the chamber is burnt.
Incredible power.
There's been an incident here!
This is the center. But where exactly did the explosion originate from?
The stony tiles, scorch marks, and general aesthetic makes this look like a dragon's lair.
Beware, beware...
Death.
Will you stop saying that?
(Check the debris.)
(Check the iron beams along the walls.)
(Check the ceiling.)
First, localize the origin point.
Could this be caused by a spell?
E-I should leave the rubble alone.
Just a quick search reveals nothing but charred rock and iron scraps.
Remnants of furniture. Shelves, maybe. Chairs.
Pushed up into the corners of the room. A violent and sudden force of heat compressed it all.
It was an instant. Then everything became nothing.
Once they stood straight, holding the ancient tunnel upright.
Askew and weak. Yet they still stand.
Yeah... it's a miracle this place hasn't collapsed entirely - you should... probably leave.
Relax. It is fine.
Your heart beats quicker.
You glance upwards, finding the somewhat high ceiling in the chamber to be scorched, but intact.
This place will stand. For now.
You look around and find the damage confusing.
While centered in the chamber, the damage appears uneven, as if the force of the explosion was struggling with itself.
With that thought, you receive a vision.
Replaying the event in your mind - an explosion.
In the chamber.
Conflagration spreading.
It just doesn't work.
However, you experiment in your head with the idea... of multiple explosions.
Suddenly it clicks.
The floor... it has several marks.
You start counting. One, two, three...
It's not enough. Looking around the chamber you see several points from which the fire clearly spread.
The explosion is... No.
Explosions.
Explosions. Multiple.
Your companion lifts his head from whatever scraps he was looking over.
What did you say?
You keep counting. Four, five, six...
Even that is not enough. Fires. The immense force.
Seven.
Eight.
You point at the last spot on the floor you can see, near the west wall where you're standing.
Nine.
Nine?
Nine of them.
You try recalling the textbook take on fireball spells, and unless there were nine individual spellcasters -- all within range mind you -- then there's only one possible explanation...
Or well. There's two. There could also be nine delayed fireball spells. Which seems equally ridiculous. But more likely...
A Necklace of Fireballs.
Nine explosions - one for each bead on a fully stocked necklace.
Exactly.
You remember it clearly, due to its historical significance.
The Assassination of Priestess Ilona, arguably the inciting spark for the Great Coast War.
Now, over a century later, you're standing here among the rubble of the very same device.
But why use such a tool of destruction here, in a tea shop on Tolstad?
Not to mention a fully potent Necklace is exceedingly rare to find these days.
The ones mass produced during the Coast War lost most of their power after the fall of their creators.
Why would someone spend a nine-beaded Necklace of Fireballs on a damn tea shop?
E-Consider what you've learned.
The goblin's gaze dances across the chamber.
You see his face contort as it dawns on him.
More than one? he mutters.
You're about to blow his little mind, aren't you?
(Hold up seven fingers.) "Nine separate explosions. Simultaneously."
It's very obvious when you think about it.
He stares at your fingers.
He won't mention it. He's too kind.
Great to hear you've got some thoughts in that helmet of yours then.
He looks around the chamber, concerned. "Walk me through it."
How do nine explosions go off at the same time?
We got a cabal of sorcerers? A coven? What?
Careful now. Do you really want to share this info with him?
The goblin is not your boss. You don't need to tell him anything.
Could be useful to keep this to yourself. For now.
Tell him, "Necklace of Fireballs."
R-"I'll... explain once we report to your lady."
Necklace of- he says and pauses.
You can see his mind working behind his sharp eyes.
Huh.
Do you think it's possible?
It's the only logical answer.
Mimic an explosion with your hands and say, "Boom."
...Like the assassination of Priestess Ilona?
Something like that.
Didn't know you were a history buff.
He nods and looks around at the destruction. "The mass produced shit they used in the Coast War... it wouldn't get close to this level of force."
He ignores your comment and looks around at the destruction. "The mass produced shit they used in the Coast War... it wouldn't get close to this level of force."
You're telling me someone tossed nine beads of fireball - essentially a fully charged and practically invaluable magic item - into a damn tea shop?
Yep.
It's that, or a group of very quick hags.
Could be an esoteric mystery as well.
The goblin smirks.
You've put the image of nine old ladies scurrying out of a burning tea shop into his mind.
Speedy hags. How horrific.
He chuckles. "If Norvik's gonna be filled with esoteric pockets of fireballs, well..."
He clicks his tongue. "Then whoever wins the election's in for a fun time."
He rubs his eyes. "Well, shit."
Another thing to report. Old Lady's not gonna believe it.
He looks you up and down. "Sure. Gotcha."
His tone implies a threat. Something like, 'If you lie to her, she'll eat you alive.'
(Leave the rubble alone.)
You are, surprisingly, confused.
You spend ten minutes simply looking around.
There's clearly damage in the center of the chamber, and the force obviously pushed everything out towards the walls.
But no matter where you look, there's no clear epicenter.
You need more time on this.
The goblin groans. "Nothing? Alright. We can take a break, or something."
He is frustrated.
There is more. Far more. The fire spreading wildly - all directions...
The center... is many.
Spells can cause most things.
Some kind of fire spell is very likely. Just look at all the burn marks!
Very obviously this chamber has been hit by a fireball spell.
Or any other type of equivalent explosive force.
He removes his sleeve from his nose and mouth. "It's a damn blast zone."
Clearly.
Any theories?
I disagree.
Do you?
He gestures around him, looking perplexed. "I... how do you... what?"
This was clearly a simple fireplace failure.
...Maybe I don't.
He stares at you, his arms still stretched out. "A fireplace filled with what?"
Fucking gunpowder?
Give him a slow nod and say, "Kids these days."
...I might need to rethink my theory.
You're right, that's ridiculous.
The goblin gives you the exact same expression you once saw on a superior officer's face, moments after you told him you wanted to open up an Urth-themed bakery.
You might.
He nods. "Yes. I am."
The goblin shakes his head.
I'll tell you what I think, Cleric.
I think - and am fairly certain of this - that a very powerful fireball spell was cast right on this spot.
Clearly.
But look, I'm no expert.
But he has good intuition.
Exactly how that would happen is confounding to me.
So let's both just look over the debris and bring as much information as we can to the Old Lady.
Great plan.
Why do you think it's a fireball?
Thanks.
He shrugs. "Pretty common spell. Powerful."
Wouldn't be the first time either. Norvik's seen its fair share of renegade wizards over the years.
Not too many capable of this kind of destruction. Not these days.
There used to be much more powerful wizards, before the start of the new era.
Back then Urth would wrestle with any rogue sorcerers.
Now that is your job.
The goblin lifts an eyebrow, and you feel a stirring in your lower stomach.
What about you? Can you cast fireball?
He asks with a little hesitation.
Are you accusing me of something, Snell?
They don't teach Fireball at the Towers.
Most clerics and paladins can't tap into arcane magics. I could. Technically.
I don't know, am I? he says, and makes a scary face.
He's attempting to make a joke. Laugh.
(Laugh heartily and pat your belly.)
I certainly hope not.
(Shake your head.) "I didn't do it."
Not. Suspicious at all.
Woah. Don't get all tough guy on me.
The goblin sighs. "Don't worry."
He points at the rubble. "Azgalist establishment run by a bird-folk. On goblin-territory?"
I don't see why a city cleric would be responsible for this.
Fair enough. But my point is: someone cast this spell. And they could be lurking around Tolstad as we speak.
Good.
The goblin smirks. "Then you can tell me if there's something off about it."
